teaser: A page-by-page tour of the Mesa Ranch observation vault: the argument, the system, the record, five graphs, and how to open and rebuild it.
core_idea: The Mesa Ranch observation desk turns Marconi's INMA deck into seventeen vault pages on synthetic records, all in one frame of menu, page and details panel; the tour explains each page, what to click and what it proves, from delta science and the atlas of 78 event types to the fractal semantic graph and the knowledge graph played in time, and ends with how to open, clone and rebuild it for another beat.

figures.caption: The vault's cover page: a menu of seventeen pages, a synthetic campus drawn in pen and ink, and a panel on the right.
Journalism is delta science, after: the landscape with a permitted power station, three data halls and four documents.
An atlas of events: twelve families around the buildout, with Power and utilities open in the panel.
A domain ontology: campus, building, construction work, source record, company and project, with six relationships.
The observations view: four headline folders, from January to September, with the full history below.
The AI workflow stepped through one cycle: observe, compare, check, report and update, with a small graph that grows.
The community impact tracker: jobs, water, power, land and public commitments, beside the draft article and two alerts.
The fractal semantic graph at level 1: the campus opens into twelve event families, with a breadcrumb back.
Every level at once: the question at the centre, then families, event types, observations and records in rings.
The knowledge graph played one observation at a time, with the new relationship at the acquisition in orange.
Sixteen synthetic records on the left, seventeen observations on the right, and the evidence lines between them.
The delta chain: observations on a time axis by entity, with an arc from each to the earlier one it was compared with.
